html:
The Second Battle of Tarain was fought in 1192 near Taraori, north of Delhi, where the Ghurid army of Muhammad of Ghor crushed the Rajput army of Prithviraj Chauhan.

A year earlier, on the same ground, Prithviraj had won and Muhammad had been wounded. Muhammad went home to Ghazni, rebuilt his army and returned. This time he used his mounted archers to harass the slower Rajput army, and a feigned retreat drew it out of order before his reserve charged. Prithviraj fled, was caught and was executed.

The result changed the map of India. With the strongest Rajput king gone, Ghurid generals took Delhi, Ajmer and then the Ganges valley as far as Bengal within a few years. One of them, Qutb ud-Din Aibak, began the Qutb Minar and in 1206 became the first ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. Muslim rule in north India lasted, in one form or another, until the Mughals fell in 1857.
sum: The Second Battle of Tarain was fought in 1192 near Taraori, north of Delhi, where the Ghurid army of Muhammad of Ghor crushed the Rajput army of Prithviraj Chauhan.
